summary.text: Casey Shepard, a Democratic attorney, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Texas's 17th District to Rep. Pete Sessions.
A seventh-generation Texan, she describes graduating from Loyola Marymount University on a debate scholarship and earning a law degree from UC Davis.
She campaigned on food and housing assistance, health-care access and government accountability.

paragraphs.text: Shepard describes herself as a seventh-generation Texan and a third-generation Central Texan, and she graduated from Midway High School.
She earned a bachelor's degree from Loyola Marymount University in 2003, where she says she went on a debate scholarship after discovering a passion for public policy debate in high school.
She earned a law degree from the University of California, Davis School of Law (Martin Luther King Jr. Hall) in 2007, and Ballotpedia lists her profession as attorney.
Shepard placed second in the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 32.4% of the vote.
She won the May 26, 2026 runoff over Jamilah Flores, who had withdrawn but remained on the ballot, 59.9% to 40.1%.
She received 46.4% of the vote to Pete Sessions's 53.6%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
